title: The three-dimensional cutoff covariance and frequency trace have exact leading Weyl coefficients

weyl_coefficients.cutoff: On normalized T3 take K_N={k in Z^3: ||k||_infinity<=N}, omega_k=sqrt(m^2+|k|^2), q_k=(2 omega_k)^(-1) and count the real covariance coordinates with the same total multiplicity as K_N
weyl_coefficients.covariance_sum: C_N=sum_(k in K_N)q_k=c_C N^2+o(N^2), where c_C=12 log((1+sqrt(3))/sqrt(2))-pi
weyl_coefficients.frequency_trace: Omega_N=sum_(k in K_N)omega_k=c_Omega N^4+o(N^4), where c_Omega=2sqrt(3)+8 log((1+sqrt(3))/sqrt(2))-pi/3
weyl_coefficients.proof_route: Lattice Riemann sums away from the origin converge to (1/2)int_([-1,1]^3)|x|^(-1)dx=c_C and int_([-1,1]^3)|x|dx=c_Omega; the singular small ball is uniform because sum_(0<|k|<=delta N)|k|^(-1)=O(delta^2N^2), and cube symmetry plus elementary face integration gives the displayed closed forms while fixed mass and the origin cell are lower order
weyl_coefficients.real_mode_guard: A real cosine/sine basis has one coordinate for k=0 and two real coordinates for each nonzero plus/minus pair, exactly the multiplicity of the full lattice sum; no extra factor two is inserted
weyl_coefficients.scope_guard: These are leading cutoff coefficients for the repository-owned normalized-torus Gaussian control, not a source normalization, renormalized energy or bounded-error lattice expansion
